title: When Large Language Models are More PersuasiveThan Incentivized Humans, and Why
abstract: arXiv:2505.09662v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have been shown to be highly persuasive, but when and why they outperform humans is still an open question. We compare the persuasiveness of two LLMs (Claude 3.5 Sonnet and DeepSeek v3) against humans who had incentives to persuade, using an interactive, real-time conversational setting. We demonstrate that LLMs persuasive superiority is context-dependent: it depends on whether the persuasion attempt is truthful (towards the right answer) or deceptive (towards the wrong answer) and on the LLM model, and wanes over repeated interactions (unlike human persuasiveness). In our first large-scale experiment, humans vs LLMs (Claude 3.5 Sonnet) interacted with other humans who were completing an online quiz for a reward, attempting to persuade them toward a given (either correct or incorrect) answer. translated_title: 当大型语言模型比受激励的人类更具说服力，以及原因
translated_abstract: 摘要：arXiv:2505.09662v4 公告类型：替换 摘要：大型语言模型（LLMs）已被证明具有高度说服力，但它们在何时以及为何超越人类仍是一个开放问题。我们在一个交互式、实时对话环境中，将两种LLMs（Claude 3.5 Sonnet和DeepSeek v3）与有激励的说服人类进行比较。我们证明，LLMs的说服优势依赖于情境：它取决于说服尝试是真实的（朝向正确答案）还是欺骗性的（朝向错误答案），以及LLM模型本身，并且在重复互动中会减弱（与人类说服力不同）。在我们的首个大规模实验中，人类与LLMs（Claude 3.5 Sonnet）与其他完成在线测验以获取奖励的人类互动，试图说服他们朝向给定（正确或错误）答案。Claude在真实和欺骗性情境中都比受激励的人类说服者更具说服力，并且其优势显著。
tldr: 本研究通过大规模交互实验发现，大型语言模型在真实和欺骗性说服情境中均优于受激励的人类，但其优势依赖上下文并随重复互动减弱。
en_tdlr: This study finds through large-scale interactive experiments that large language models outperform incentivized humans in both truthful and deceptive persuasion, but their advantage is context-dependent and diminishes over repeated interactions.
